newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee slips on dlr speculation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee slips on dlr speculation.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which had risen earlier due to high call rates, lost ground as speculators bought dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.80 to the dollar, after opening at 57.85, and rising to 57.72. The rupee closed at 57.87 on Monday.
"The rupee rose to 57.72 when banks began selling dollars after call rates rose," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
The U.S. currency however, recovered as speculators began buying dollars, expecting the currency to rise on its overseas strength, he said.
Overnight call money closed at 20 percent, after moving between 15 and 20 percent, dealers said.
"Money was bit tight since banks had bought dollars from the Central Bank, but today's rise was more due to a mismatch between borrowers and lenders," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
